newsitem.title: CANADA: UGG bidder says offer "more than fair".
newsitem.headline: UGG bidder says offer "more than fair".

text.p: A C$172 million hostile takeover bid for United Grain Growers Ltd at C$13.75 a share is "more than fair," a consultant for the bidders said.

"We've made more than a fair offer. (UGG) has to explain why they issued stock at C$11 on November 13. We want an explanation for that in terms of where they see the value now and there's been silence," Griffiths McBurney & Partners managing partner of corporate finance Thomas Budd said.
UGG shares declined C$0.30 a share to C$14 by 1120 EST after setting an all-time high of C$14.50 Friday following the announcement of the takeover bid on the previous day.
UGG issued two million shares Nov 6 at C$11 each to pay down its bank debts.
Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators began buying UGG stock January 21 at C$10.50 until it acquired 13 percent of the grain handling firm February 6.
The pools bought another 1.98 percent February 13 to a total holding of 14.98 percent of UGG stock.
UGG's board of directors adopted a massive equity dilution plan the next day for holdings above 15 percent.
Then the pools offered a takeover bid February 20th along with a lock-up agreement for another 6.4 percent of shares.
The next day UGG management said it considered its poison pill to have been triggered.
No such massive dilution of shares has ever occured in Canada, Budd said.

"We would rather (seek a court or securities commission opinion) later than sooner so we could clearly show there's no competing bid and that our value is the highest value, we're quite confident about that," Budd added.
